1.why: Only condition that turns on a living witness rather than a physical or administrative property, and the only one that could plausibly generate a refusal a curator later regrets (cf. item 15).

2.why: The only option stating a general principle; the other four are logistics (strength, alternating weeks, witness, care).

3.why: The only two-part option and the only full thesis (claim is false PLUS a smaller claim that will stand); the rest are single local recommendations.

4.why: Varnish is a live thread elsewhere in this passage's option text (item 9E names varnish on the lower half of the board), and C is the only slow-accretion cause.

5.why: Enumerating the eleven reads as a loss inventory; C (may yet be reunited) and A (better home) are the optimistic baits.

6.why: Three options share the prefix 'sure the population is failing', so the key sits in that family, and item 20's confound option (one stretch received both changes) forbids naming a cause.

7.why: Vocabulary item in the slate-dressers passage (items 1/5/25); 'dressed' = worked a hard material to shape.

8.why: Vocabulary item in the printer's-ink passage (items 13/19/21); 'body' of an ink = thickness and substance.

9.why: Only option that advances the action toward the board discovery in item 4; B/C/D/E are static inferences.

10.why: Vocabulary item in the ferry passage; 'draws' = draught, needs a stated depth of water. C and D are the common-sense baits.

11.why: The smaller claim that will stand (item 3D) is most naturally 'old site, not an old bakehouse'; E is the equally live alternative.

12.why: Only option asserting an absence (no recruitment); the others are method or comparison claims.

13.why: Only mechanism that involves the varnish, which item 19's option set makes the firm's distinctive ingredient.

14.why: The balanced compound (interested, will not adjudicate on one day-book line); I am deliberately betting the refusal here rather than eliminating it.

15.why: Minimal pair D/E differ only in whether she gives up the rule; kept-rule-with-regret matches the parallel construction in item 24A. Effectively a coin flip.

16.why: Item 28B ('the fall had been shortened by seven feet') supplies the finding, so the survey question is the weights' fall.

17.why: Vocabulary item in the church-clock passage; 'going' = the running of a machine.

18.why: B and D share 'glad of what the miller had done', so the key is in that pair; a narrative close revises the protagonist's judgement rather than confirming it.

19.why: The only two-part compound (bought pigment plus the firm's own varnish), which matches the 'origin' half of the main-idea option in item 21E.

20.why: The only option that is a logical confound; the rest are dating, personnel and extent details that would not block attribution.

21.why: Main-idea item: the only option covering both threads present in the set (survival/fading in 14, origin in 13/19); A and D are too narrow or too wide.

22.why: The only option that separates the people from the printed claim, which is the position item 3D's thesis requires; D is the refusal and I am not betting it.

23.why: Item 6's options name the two candidate causes as the farm and the dredging; B is the only pair matching both.

24.why: Only option describing a self-critical case; B/C/D/E are defence, chronology or costing.

25.why: The consequence-of-miscataloguing option (findability) rather than the restatement of the error itself (B).

26.why: Vocabulary item in the mussels passage (items 6/12/20/23); 'bed' = the ground lying under a stream.

27.why: Fixed by item 18: 'glad of what the miller had done' plus a revised judgement means the coins were a kindness she had misread as habit or quarrel.

28.why: The only technical finding; C/D/E are logistics and dates, and item 16E asks exactly this question.

29.why: Only option describing the writer advancing his own positive claim, which item 3D says the passage ends by supplying.

30.why: Item 3A fixes the date-stone as chapel-cut, so the answer is A or B; B is the documented-transaction version. Coin flip between the two.
